summary.title: Hello Auth - secured login app
summary.description: React SPA + Spring Boot API with server-side sessions (Spring Session JDBC). Scope: registration, login/lockout/IP throttling, logout, password reset, admin user management, admin bootstrap. Branch seahjunsheng.

data.name: Spring Boot API

threats.title: Vulnerable third-party dependency
threats.description: A known CVE in a Spring, Hibernate, H2, PostgreSQL driver, React or Vite dependency is exploited.
threats.mitigation:
Current releases were chosen (Spring Boot 4.1.1, React 19.3, Vite 8) and npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities. Add automated SCA (dependency-vuln-scan / Dependabot) to CI and patch on a schedule.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

threats.title: Volumetric denial of service
threats.description: Floods of requests exhaust threads, database connections or CPU (every login costs a BCrypt comparison).
threats.mitigation:
The app limits failed logins per IP and reset requests per IP, but has no global rate limit. Put a WAF or gateway rate limit and a request-size limit in front of the API.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

data.name: Application database
data.description: users, password_reset_tokens, SPRING_SESSION tables.

threats.title: Database contents stolen
threats.description: An attacker with read access to the database or a backup obtains credentials or reset tokens.
threats.mitigation: Passwords are BCrypt (cost 12, minimum 12 characters); reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes of 256 random bits; no plaintext secrets are stored. Encryption at rest and network isolation of the database are deployment controls.

data.name: Audit log
data.description: AUDIT logger output shipped to the log platform.

data.name: Email service
data.description: Delivers password reset emails (logging stub in dev).

threats.title: Credentials or session cookie intercepted in transit
threats.description: An attacker on the network reads passwords or the SESSION cookie in transit between the browser and the API.
threats.mitigation: TLS terminated at the proxy in prod; session cookie Secure with the __Host- prefix (application-prod.yml, SessionCookieConfig); HSTS sent on HTTPS by Spring Security defaults. Local dev over HTTP is the PRD's accepted gap.

threats.title: Reset email read in transit or in the mailbox
threats.description: Email is not end-to-end encrypted; anyone who can read the recipient's mail can use the reset link.
threats.mitigation:
Accepted residual risk: the token is single-use, expires after 30 minutes, newer requests revoke older links, and the account owner can reset again. Use a provider that enforces TLS for SMTP.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: With the real EmailService.

threats.title: Secrets exposed through environment configuration
threats.description: DATABASE_PASSWORD and APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD are plain environment variables and can leak through process listings, orchestrator dumps or CI logs.
threats.mitigation:
No secret has a default in the repository and startup fails without them. Source them from AWS Secrets Manager or Vault, restrict who can read the deployment environment, and rotate the bootstrap admin password after first start.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

diagrams.title: Level 0 - System context
diagrams.description: The browser SPA, the API behind a TLS proxy, its database, the audit log and the email provider.

data.name: Visitor / User
data.description: Anonymous or authenticated USER.

threats.title: Credential stuffing / password spraying across many IPs
threats.description: A botnet tries breached passwords against many accounts, staying under the per-IP limit.
threats.mitigation:
Per-account lockout caps guesses per account (5 per 15 minutes) and the password minimum is 12 characters. MFA is out of the PRD's scope. Next steps: check new passwords against a breached-password list and add a gateway/WAF bot defence.

Owner: Backend. Timeline: Next iteration.

threats.title: User denies performing an action
threats.description: A user claims they did not sign in, reset a password or register.
threats.mitigation: AUDIT log records USER_REGISTERED, LOGIN_SUCCEEDED/FAILED, LOGOUT and PASSWORD_RESET_* with username and IP (AuditLoggingIntegrationTests).

data.name: Admin
data.description: Authenticated ADMIN.

threats.title: Admin account takeover without MFA
threats.description: A phished or guessed admin password grants full user management.
threats.mitigation:
Lockout, IP throttling, the 12-character minimum and session revocation on password reset reduce the risk. MFA / step-up for ADMIN is explicitly out of the PRD's scope (also IM8 ac-2); add TOTP or WebAuthn for admins before a real deployment.

Owner: Product owner. Timeline: Before production.

threats.title: Admin denies a privileged change
threats.description: An admin claims they did not disable, demote or delete an account.
threats.mitigation: USER_ENABLED / USER_DISABLED / USER_ROLE_CHANGED (from/to) / USER_DELETED are logged with actor and target, plus ADMIN_ACTION_REJECTED for self-actions.

data.name: Email service
data.description: Real provider in prod; LoggingEmailService in dev.

data.name: Operator config
data.description: Environment variables, application-prod.yml.

data.name: React SPA
data.description: frontend/src; all calls via api/client.ts.

threats.title: XSS steals the session
threats.description: Injected script reads the session cookie or acts as the user.
threats.mitigation: The session cookie is HttpOnly; React escapes all output and there are no HTML sinks; the build ships a strict CSP with no unsafe-inline/eval. Residual: script running in the page could still call the API with the in-memory CSRF token, so CSP and output encoding remain essential.

threats.title: Error details shown to users
threats.description: A rendering error or console output reveals internal details.
threats.mitigation: An error boundary renders a generic message only; console output is limited to development builds and stripped from production bundles.

threats.title: Clickjacking the SPA
threats.description: The SPA is framed by a malicious site to trick clicks (for example on admin Delete).
threats.mitigation:
The API sends frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options DENY; the SPA's meta CSP cannot carry frame-ancestors. The web server hosting dist/ must send the headers configured in vite.config.ts preview.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

threats.title: Open redirect after sign-in
threats.description: A crafted 'from' location sends users to an attacker site after login.
threats.mitigation: GuestOnly only follows same-app paths (safeRedirectTarget rejects '//host' and absolute URLs).

threats.title: Reset token leaks from the URL
threats.description: The token in the reset link leaks through Referer headers, server logs or browser history.
threats.mitigation: The token travels in the URL fragment (never sent to servers), the page removes it from the address bar after reading it, and index.html sets referrer policy no-referrer.

data.name: TLS reverse proxy
data.description: Terminates TLS; sets X-Forwarded-*. Deployment infrastructure.

threats.title: Weak TLS configuration at the edge
threats.description: Outdated protocols or ciphers at the proxy weaken transport security.
threats.mitigation:
Out of the application's control: enforce TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers, HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect and CA-signed certificates at the proxy.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

data.name: Security filter chain
data.description: CORS, Spring Session, CSRF, authorization, logout.

threats.title: Cross-site request forgery
threats.description: A malicious site makes the victim's browser perform a state-changing request with the ambient session cookie.
threats.mitigation: Synchronizer-token CSRF on every POST/PATCH/DELETE including login and logout (SecurityConfig, CsrfTokenRepository in the session); SameSite=Strict cookie; tests assert 403 without a token.

threats.title: Other origins read the CSRF token or API data
threats.description: A malicious origin calls GET /api/auth/csrf with credentials and reads the token.
threats.mitigation: CORS allow-list of exact origins (wildcards rejected at startup) with credentials; other origins get 403 (WebSecurityIntegrationTests.corsRejectsOtherOrigins).

threats.title: Session fixation
threats.description: An attacker plants a session ID before the victim logs in and then reuses it.
threats.mitigation: Session ID changes at login (ChangeSessionIdAuthenticationStrategy in SessionLogin); CSRF token rotated (LoginIntegrationTests.loginChangesTheSessionIdToPreventFixation).

threats.title: Session hijacking window
threats.description: A stolen or unattended session stays usable while it is kept active, because sessions have no absolute lifetime.
threats.mitigation:
Server sessions expire after 15 minutes idle and the SPA signs out after 15 minutes without input (useIdleTimeout); the cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict; logout, password reset, disable, role change and delete revoke sessions. Remaining: add an absolute session lifetime (for example 8 hours).

Owner: Backend. Timeline: Next iteration.

threats.title: Unauthenticated or non-admin access to protected endpoints
threats.description: A USER or anonymous caller reaches /api/admin/** or other protected endpoints.
threats.mitigation: URL rules end in denyAll(); /api/admin/** needs ROLE_ADMIN and the controller adds @PreAuthorize; roles come only from the server-side session (AdminIntegrationTests.userRoleGets403OnEveryAdminEndpoint).

threats.title: Probing leaves no audit trail
threats.description: Probing for admin endpoints or forged cross-site requests goes unnoticed.
threats.mitigation: Every 403 (role or CSRF failure) is audited as ACCESS_DENIED with actor, IP, method and path (ProblemJsonSecurityHandlers; AuditLoggingIntegrationTests). 401s are not audited because anonymous page loads produce them. A request correlation ID is not yet propagated.

threats.title: Error responses leak internals
threats.description: Stack traces or exception messages reveal implementation details.
threats.mitigation: server.error.include-message/stacktrace=never; every error is an RFC 9457 problem with curated text; unexpected errors return a generic 500; only actuator health is exposed.

data.name: Auth endpoints
data.description: register, login, /api/me (AuthController, LoginService).

threats.title: Username enumeration through login
threats.description: Responses or timing reveal whether a username exists, is locked or disabled.
threats.mitigation: One 401 body for unknown user, wrong password, locked and disabled; every path does one BCrypt comparison (dummy hash for unknown/locked). Residual: known accounts add a small database write.

threats.title: Online password guessing against one account
threats.description: An attacker guesses a user's password, including with parallel requests.
threats.mitigation: Lockout after 5 consecutive failures within 15 minutes, for 15 minutes; attempts are reserved under a row lock so 20 parallel guesses evaluate exactly 5 (LockoutIntegrationTests).

threats.title: Attacker locks out a legitimate user
threats.description: Five wrong passwords from a single source lock the victim's account for 15 minutes (the per-IP limit is 20).
threats.mitigation:
Lockout is temporary, cleared by password reset, and a throttled IP cannot extend it. Stricter option: throttle an (IP, username) pair below the lockout threshold so only several sources together can lock an account; trade-off documented in docs/design.md.

Owner: Product owner. Timeline: Decide before submission.

threats.title: BCrypt 72-byte truncation
threats.description: BCrypt ignores bytes past 72, so a long password plus any suffix would match.
threats.mitigation: Passwords over 72 bytes are rejected at registration/reset and never match at login (LoginIntegrationTests.passwordBeyondBcryptsLimitNeverMatchesByTruncation).

threats.title: Mass assignment of role at registration
threats.description: A client sends role=ADMIN or enabled flags in the registration body.
threats.mitigation: RegisterRequest only binds username, email and password; the service always creates role USER.

threats.title: Account enumeration through registration
threats.description: 409 conflicts reveal that a username or email is registered.
threats.mitigation:
Required by the PRD (clear conflict error). Limit it with a registration rate limit or CAPTCHA.

Owner: Backend. Timeline: Next iteration.

threats.title: Automated mass registration
threats.description: Bots create large numbers of accounts.
threats.mitigation:
No registration throttle yet. Add a per-IP limit (reuse AttemptThrottle) and bot protection at the gateway.

Owner: Backend. Timeline: Next iteration.

data.name: Password reset
data.description: request (async issue) and confirm.

threats.title: Account enumeration through reset requests
threats.description: Different responses or timing reveal whether an email is registered.
threats.mitigation: Always 202 with the same body; lookup, token issue and email run asynchronously so timing is identical (PasswordResetIntegrationTests.responseIsIdenticalWhetherOrNotTheEmailIsRegistered).

threats.title: Reset token guessing or reuse
threats.description: An attacker guesses a token, replays a used one, or redeems it twice concurrently.
threats.mitigation: 256-bit random tokens; SHA-256 hash stored; 30-minute expiry; single use enforced under a row lock; a new request deletes older unused tokens (PasswordResetIntegrationTests).

threats.title: Email flooding a victim's inbox
threats.description: Repeated reset requests flood a victim with emails.
threats.mitigation: 5 requests per IP per 15 minutes (429 + Retry-After). Residual: distributed requests; add a per-account cap if abuse appears.

threats.title: Old sessions survive a password reset
threats.description: An attacker who stole a session keeps access after the victim resets the password.
threats.mitigation: All sessions of the user are deleted after commit (SessionRevoker; PasswordResetIntegrationTests.resetInvalidatesEveryExistingSessionOfTheUser).

data.name: Admin user management
data.description: /api/admin/users/**.

threats.title: Demoted admin keeps admin rights
threats.description: Authorities cached in an existing session outlive a role change.
threats.mitigation: Role change, disable and delete revoke the target's sessions after commit (AdminIntegrationTests.roleChangesTakeEffectImmediately).

threats.title: Admin locks everyone out
threats.description: An admin disables, demotes or deletes their own account and no admin remains.
threats.mitigation: Self-actions are rejected with 409; bootstrap seeds a new admin when no enabled admin exists.

threats.title: Two admins disable or demote each other concurrently
threats.description: Both requests pass the self-check and succeed, leaving no enabled admin.
threats.mitigation:
Recoverable without database edits (restart with unused APP_ADMIN_USERNAME/EMAIL). To close it, lock both actor and target rows in a fixed order and re-check the actor inside the transaction.

Owner: Backend. Timeline: Next iteration.

threats.title: Admin views of personal data go unrecorded
threats.description: GET /api/admin/users returns every email address.
threats.mitigation: Each listing is audited as USER_LIST_VIEWED with actor, IP, page and size.

data.name: Hello
data.description: /api/hello returns text/plain.

threats.title: Greeting reflects attacker-controlled input
threats.description: The username is echoed back and could carry script.
threats.mitigation: Usernames are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-]; the response is text/plain with nosniff and CSP default-src 'none'; React escapes it.

data.name: Admin bootstrap
data.description: ApplicationRunner at startup.

threats.title: Default or weak admin credential
threats.description: The bootstrap admin keeps the operator-supplied password indefinitely.
threats.mitigation:
There is no default password, the policy is enforced and startup fails without one. The password is not forced to change at first login (IM8 ac-6): rotate it via password reset after first start, or add a forced-change flag.

Owner: Backend. Timeline: Next iteration.

threats.title: Bootstrap takes over an existing account
threats.description: An attacker registers 'admin' first and is promoted when the bootstrap runs.
threats.mitigation: Bootstrap never reuses an existing username or email; it fails startup instead (AdminBootstrapIntegrationTests.neverTakesOverTheConfiguredAccountEvenIfItIsADisabledAdmin).

data.name: IP throttle (in memory)
data.description: Caffeine map of attempts per client IP.

threats.title: Throttle memory exhaustion
threats.description: Requests from many distinct IPs grow the throttle map without bound.
threats.mitigation: Caffeine cache bounded to 100,000 keys with expiry after the window.

threats.title: Throttle state not shared across instances
threats.description: With several API instances, each keeps its own counters, multiplying the per-IP allowance; a restart resets them.
threats.mitigation:
Move to a shared store (Redis / Bucket4j) before running more than one instance.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: When scaling out.

data.name: users
data.description: Username, email, BCrypt hash, role, enabled, lockout state.

threats.title: SQL injection
threats.description: Crafted input alters queries against the users table.
threats.mitigation: Spring Data JPA with JPQL named parameters only; no native or concatenated SQL.

threats.title: Offline cracking of stolen hashes
threats.description: Password hashes from a breach are cracked offline.
threats.mitigation: BCrypt cost 12 with a 12-character minimum makes offline cracking slow.

data.name: password_reset_tokens
data.description: SHA-256 token hash, expiry, used_at.

data.name: SPRING_SESSION
data.description: Session IDs and serialized SecurityContext + CSRF token.

threats.title: Tampered session data deserialized
threats.description: Spring Session JDBC stores attributes with Java serialization; anyone able to write SPRING_SESSION_ATTRIBUTES could plant a malicious serialized object.
threats.mitigation:
Requires database write access. Keep the app's DB account least-privileged and the DB network-isolated; optionally switch Spring Session to a JSON (Jackson) serializer.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

threats.title: Session store read to hijack sessions
threats.description: Session IDs read from the store are replayed.
threats.mitigation: The store holds no passwords; access requires database credentials; sessions expire after 15 minutes idle and are cleaned up every minute.

data.name: Audit log
data.description: AUDIT logger; ECS JSON on stdout in prod.

threats.title: Audit log tampering or loss
threats.description: An attacker or operator edits or deletes audit lines; logs on local stdout are lost.
threats.mitigation:
Ship ECS JSON logs to an append-only central store with restricted delete rights and a retention policy.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

threats.title: Log forging through user input
threats.description: A username containing newlines forges extra audit lines.
threats.mitigation: AuditLog escapes control characters, quotes and backslashes and truncates values (AuditLogTests); JSON encoding in prod escapes as well.

threats.title: Secrets written to logs
threats.description: Passwords or tokens appear in logs.
threats.mitigation: No audit field accepts secrets; request DTOs redact toString(); validation errors never echo values; attempted unknown usernames are not logged (AuditLoggingIntegrationTests asserts no password in output).

threats.title: Spoofed X-Forwarded-For evades the IP throttle
threats.description: An attacker sends their own X-Forwarded-For so every attempt appears to come from a new IP.
threats.mitigation: The app uses request.getRemoteAddr(). In prod, server.forward-headers-strategy=native makes Tomcat honour X-Forwarded-For only from internal proxy addresses; dev ignores the header entirely.

threats.title: Reset link written to logs
threats.description: The dev email stub logs the full reset link, a live credential.
threats.mitigation: Required by the PRD's stub; LoggingEmailService is @Profile("!prod") so production cannot start without a real EmailService.

threats.title: No privacy notice at collection
threats.description: Users are not told how their email and sign-in activity are used and retained.
threats.mitigation:
Add a short privacy notice on the registration page (PDPA notification).

Owner: Frontend. Timeline: Before production.

data.name: Admin
data.description: Sees every account's email address.

data.name: Spring Boot API
data.description: Collects and processes personal data.

data.name: users
data.description: Username and email per account.

threats.title: No retention or self-service deletion
threats.description: Accounts and personal data are kept indefinitely; users cannot delete their own account.
threats.mitigation:
Define retention; admins can delete accounts today. Add self-service deletion/export if required.

Owner: Product owner. Timeline: Next iteration.

threats.title: Stored personal data identifies individuals
threats.description: A breach of the users table identifies people by email.
threats.mitigation: Only username and email are collected (data minimisation); no other profile data.

data.name: Audit log
data.description: Usernames and client IPs per security event.

threats.title: Audit records link usernames to IP addresses
threats.description: Security logs let usernames be linked to network locations over time.
threats.mitigation:
Needed for security monitoring. Define a retention period and restrict log access; emails and unknown usernames are never logged.

Owner: Platform. Timeline: Before production.

threats.title: Registration reveals whether an email is registered
threats.description: Anyone can learn that a person has an account by trying to register their email.
threats.mitigation:
Required by the PRD. Rate-limit registration; login and reset do not leak existence.

Owner: Product owner. Timeline: Accepted.

threats.title: Admins see every user's email address
threats.description: The admin list returns all emails, more than most admin tasks need.
threats.mitigation:
PRD Story 8 requires the email in the list. Consider masking with an explicit, audited reveal.

Owner: Product owner. Timeline: Next iteration.
